summary: The owner's creation and fire myth (book/creation.md and the First Book): the mason's line dropped the six unlit coals from the highest point of the island, and the snowflake coal took fire in the air (I-0027a); the summit is called after the kindred Binnean a' Chlachair, the Mason's Point. The map's highest ground is the moor of the central massif at height 51, the greatest in the grid (39 cells at 50 or more, all in the Doire uaine hills between Tobar dhìreach and the warm springs). Appendix I puts the island's highest ground above Muileann gheal (burg 493), so the summit is set on the height-51 cell just north-east of that town (grid cell 4977, pack cell 2745), clear of the markers already on the moor (the warm springs, the Hollow Man, the meeting of the cups). It is added as a marker of its own, the next free id, 48; no other layer names peaks.

value.name: Binnean a' Chlachair
value.note: Binnean a' Chlachair, the Mason's Point: the highest ground of Rodos, a little under three thousand six hundred feet, on the bare moor above Muileann gheal in the Doire uaine hills. The Line of the Mason tells that Fearghas of that line carried the six unlit coals up here and let them fall, and that the coal flecked with white stars took fire in the air as it fell. The summit has borne the kindred's name since. Herders of Muileann gheal leave a stone on the top when they pass, and none will light a fire there.

map_edits.why: I-0027a: Fearghas of the Mason's line lets the six unlit coals fall from the highest ground of the island, above where Muileann gheal now stands, and the snowflake coal takes fire in the air; the summit is called Binnean a' Chlachair. The point is the grid point of cell 4977 (height 51).
